title: Marrakech, Morocco
overview: Marrakech, the 'Red City', is Morocco's most magical destination – a sensory explosion of spice-laden souks, intricately tiled palaces, and vibrant Djemaa el-Fna square. The medina (old city), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, has barely changed in centuries, with narrow labyrinthine alleys leading to hidden riads, ornate mosques, and hammams. A short flight from Europe, Marrakech offers extraordinary value and an immersive cultural experience unlike anywhere else.
best_time_to_visit: March–May and October–November for pleasant temperatures (20–28°C). Summer (June–August) is extremely hot (38–42°C). December–February is cool with possible rain but festive atmosphere.
climate: Semi-arid. Very hot, dry summers (38–42°C), mild winters (5–18°C). Rain is rare and mostly in winter. Low humidity in summer.

attractions.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square
attractions.description: Marrakech's beating heart – by day, snake charmers and orange juice stalls; by evening, transforms into a vast open-air theatre with storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Free to wander; food stalls ~$5-10.

attractions.name: Medina Souks
attractions.description: Miles of covered markets organised by trade: spice souk, leather souk, lantern souk, textile souk. Expert navigation required. Bargain hard – start at 25-30% of asking price.

attractions.name: Majorelle Garden & YSL Museum
attractions.description: Stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle, later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. The adjacent Berber Museum is excellent.

attractions.name: Bahia Palace
attractions.description: 19th-century palace showcasing the finest of Moroccan and Islamic architecture: painted cedar ceilings, zellij tiling, and carved stucco. Affordable and impressive.

attractions.name: Hammam Experience
attractions.description: Traditional Moroccan bathhouse ritual – steam room, black soap scrub, and a clay mask. Authentic hammams cost $5-10; upscale spa versions $50-100.

attractions.name: Saadian Tombs
attractions.description: Elaborate royal tombs from the Saadian dynasty, rediscovered in 1917, with intricate tilework and carved plaster. Low entry price.

attractions.name: Medersa Ben Youssef
attractions.description: Morocco's largest Quranic school, built in the 14th century. The central courtyard's carved stucco and mosaic tilework are among the finest examples of Moroccan craftsmanship.

attractions.name: Day Trip to Atlas Mountains
attractions.description: One-hour drive to the Ourika Valley or Toubkal National Park. Highest peak in North Africa (4,167m). Guided day hikes, Berber village visits.

food.name: Tagine
food.description: Slow-cooked stew in a conical clay pot – lamb with prunes and almonds, or chicken with preserved lemon. Ubiquitous and excellent. Good riads serve the best versions.

food.name: Couscous Friday
food.description: By Moroccan tradition, couscous is served every Friday. Find it at local restaurants away from tourist areas for an authentic experience.

food.name: Street Food at Djemaa el-Fna
food.description: Merguez sausages, harira soup, snail broth, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Busy and atmospheric evening dining.

food.name: Mint Tea Ceremony
food.description: Moroccan hospitality ritual poured from height into small glasses. Sweet and refreshing. Often offered in shops as a social gesture.

food.name: Le Jardin or Nomad (Medina)
food.description: Upscale Moroccan-fusion rooftop restaurants near the medina. Excellent views, refined tagines, and cocktails.

transport: The medina is best explored on foot (or getting pleasantly lost). Petits taxis are metered for short rides (~$2-5). A horse-drawn calèche is a romantic alternative for a tour of the ramparts. Marrakech Menara Airport is 6km from the city centre – taxi ~$7.

budget_guide.notes: Marrakech is excellent value. A traditional riad with breakfast can cost less than a budget hotel in Europe. Always negotiate taxi fares before getting in.

tips: Hire a licensed guide for the souks to avoid harassment and learn the history.
Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees) in the medina out of respect.
Accept mint tea offerings graciously in shops – it doesn't obligate you to buy.
Learn a few words of Darija (Moroccan Arabic) or French – greatly appreciated.
The medina is deliberately confusing – getting lost is part of the experience; use Google Maps to re-orient.
